parent.title: A routed one-week Greece plan from an Athens arrival, summer 2026

siblings.title: Athens non-negotiables: the summer 2026 field manual
siblings.summary: Book the 08:00 Acropolis slot, pair it with the Acropolis Museum and the Ancient Agora, and treat almost everything else in Athens as optional.

siblings.title: After Athens: Greek island clusters compared for a 3-5 day August 2026 tail
siblings.summary: For a 3-5 day tail after Athens in August 2026, one Cyclades island (Naxos or Milos) beats any two-island hop.

siblings.title: Day trips from Athens without changing base — summer 2026
siblings.summary: One spare day in August: take the early hydrofoil to Hydra, or Delphi if you want antiquity — and skip Meteora and the three-island cruise entirely.

siblings.title: Athens to the islands, summer 2026: ferries, ports and when to fly instead
siblings.summary: Piraeus, Rafina or Lavrio, conventional ferry or catamaran, and the small set of legs where a domestic flight actually beats the boat in August 2026.

siblings.title: Eating and Drinking in Athens and the Islands, Summer 2026
siblings.summary: Route Athens around souvlaki row, one mezedopoleio dinner and one rooftop; skip the starred night unless you want it.

sources.title: Meteora monasteries — opening hours and days
sources.claim: Each of the six Meteora monasteries closes on a different weekday; summer hours run 1 April-31 October and entry is EUR 5 cash per monastery with a strict dress code.

sources.title: Meteora train restorations and express bus solutions
sources.claim: The Athens-Kalambaka rail line has been out since the 2023 Daniel storm; Hellenic Train runs a train to Paleofarsalos then a connecting bus, with full rail restoration promised by late 2026.

sources.title: Athens to Delphi and Meteora
sources.claim: Athens-Delphi is 2.5-3h by car, Athens-Meteora 3.5-4h, Delphi-Meteora about 3.5h over mountain roads; Delphi works as a day trip while Meteora needs at least one overnight and has no direct train.

sources.title: Peloponnese road trip itinerary
sources.claim: Core Peloponnese driving legs: Athens-Corinth ~1.5h, Corinth-Nafplio ~1h, Nafplio-Mycenae and Nafplio-Epidaurus 30 min each, Areopoli-Kalamata under 2h, Kalamata-Pylos ~1h, Pylos-Olympia under 2h.

sources.title: Greece heatwave, July 2026
sources.claim: In the July 2026 heatwave central Greece hit 43.5C and the eastern Peloponnese 41-42C while Aegean islands sat at 28-30C under the meltemi, and the Acropolis shut noon-5pm.

sources.title: Greece motorway tolls
sources.claim: Greek motorway tolls were revised in January 2026: Athens-Corinth on the A8 runs EUR 13.80-19.50 and Corinth-Tripoli-Kalamata on the Moreas A7 about EUR 11.75, with e-pass discounts of 8-15%.

sources.title: How much does a trip to Greece cost
sources.claim: Greece 2026 budgets: EUR 70-250 per person per day; rooms EUR 80-150 on mid-tier/mainland vs EUR 150-280 on Santorini and Mykonos in July-August; small hire car EUR 25-50/day.

sources.title: Our road trip to Mani and beyond
sources.claim: Athens-Kardamyli is 273 km / about 3h17, Athens-Areopoli 295 km / 3h20, and Mani back roads average only ~60 km/h; the region needs 3-4 days and July-August is the worst time.

sources.title: Rick Steves forum — Peloponnese road trip, 4-5 days
sources.claim: Rick Steves forum consensus on a 4.5-day Peloponnese loop: cut stops, base in Nafplio, and Mani/Areopoli is not realistically a day trip.

sources.title: Opening hours and entrance fees for Greek archaeological sites
sources.claim: Summer entrance fees: Mycenae, Epidaurus, Olympia and Delphi EUR 12 each, Ancient Corinth EUR 8, with sites generally open 08:00-19:30 in summer.

sources.title: Visiting Mystras
sources.claim: Mystras costs EUR 20 in summer, opens 08:00-20:00 from 1 April to 31 August, needs about two hours and is a steep climb from the lower gate.

sources.title: Epidaurus Festival 2026
sources.claim: The Epidaurus Festival 2026 runs 20 June to 29 August at the Ancient Theatre, with August weekend performances including Antigone (7-8 Aug), Lysistrata (21-22 Aug) and Ion (28-29 Aug).

sources.title: Voidokilia beach guide
sources.claim: Voidokilia is free and unorganised - no sunbeds, umbrellas or canteen - reached by a dirt road and 5-minute dune walk, and is busiest 11:00-18:00 in July and August.

sources.title: Elafonisos ferry schedule and tickets
sources.claim: The Pounta-Elafonisos car ferry crosses in 8-10 minutes, runs roughly every 30 minutes from 07:00 to after 23:00 in July, and costs EUR 2 per adult plus EUR 12 per car.

sources.title: Best time to visit Meteora
sources.claim: Meteora in July-August is high-crowd and high-heat; the guidance is one night minimum, two nights ideal, visiting monasteries early and returning at sunset.

sources.title: Zagori complete guide
sources.claim: Meteora to Zagori takes about 3 hours over narrow two-lane mountain roads, and Zagori itself wants three days.

sources.title: Car rental in Greece
sources.claim: August car hire in Greece runs EUR 50-100 per day for a compact, zero-deductible insurance adds EUR 5-12 per day, and mainland petrol is about EUR 2.00-2.10 per litre in 2026.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Piraeus to Santorini
sources.claim: Piraeus-Santorini ferries start at EUR 46.50 and take 4h45 to over 11 hours, with up to 8 daily summer crossings that sell out fast in high season.

sources.title: Trippy — Athens to Volos distance
sources.claim: Athens to Volos, the gateway to Pelion, is about 328 km and 3h25 of driving.

sources.title: Trippy — Volos to Kalambaka distance
sources.claim: Kalambaka (Meteora) to Volos is about 140 km and just over 2 hours of driving.

sources.title: Vriskoapostasi — Nafplio to Monemvasia route
sources.claim: Nafplio to Monemvasia is 231 km / 3h29 with EUR 8.55 of tolls; splitting it via Mystras gives Nafplio-Mystras 127 km / 2h07 and Mystras-Monemvasia 93 km / 1h53.
